payload.goal: Automate the session handoff sofar already makes content-complete: a stateless driver (sofar drive <initiative>) that runs an initiative task-by-task through fresh agent sessions, records every handoff as events in the record, and reaches any headless agent through a three-call adapter (launch, usage, wait) — Claude Code first, a second adapter to prove the contract. The record is the queue; the driver holds no state of its own.

payload.because: The next session reads CLAUDE.md and the standing constraints, not the chat where the ruling was given, and obeys them verbatim (drift-certification measures exactly that) — so a ruling that is not in the record is enforced against the work by sofar itself. Recorded honestly about currency: the driver is operator-efficient, not token-efficient; each handoff re-reads the record on a cold cache, so a driven run spends more tokens than the manual one for the same work and buys hours and consistency instead. The two clauses kept are what distinguish sofar from another agent product with a billing surface.
payload.chose: Guard-rails yield to efficiency: a feature that makes sofar more token-, feature- or performance-efficient may deviate from a CLAUDE.md guard-rail, provided the deviation is logged as a Decision that names the rail it supersedes. First application: the launch clause of SPEC §Architectural invariants is superseded — sofar may launch the operator's own agent process (claude, codex, opencode…) under the operator's own auth. Kept intact, deliberately: sofar holds no API keys, never infers, and never sends user content off the machine — the driver needs none of those. Ruled by the user 2026-08-27; this supersedes felt-cost D3's reading only as far as process launch.
payload.over: Keeping the driver outside packages/engine as a user-side script or a separate package; or reading "sofar never calls a model" as forbidding process launch and shipping only the sensor hook.
payload.rule: sofar may launch the operator's own agent process under the operator's auth, but it never holds API keys, never infers, and never sends user content off the machine; any further guard-rail deviation must be logged as a Decision naming the rail it supersedes before the work proceeds.

payload.because: Sofar's record is already agent-agnostic (JSONL + MCP + CLI), so only the trigger and the spawn are Claude-Code-shaped; designing those against the record instead of against hooks is what makes the driver portable, resumable and auditable — two driver implementations can pick up the same run. Usage reporting is the least portable thing across vendors, so the model-agnostic policy must not depend on it. Building the agent loop is building Cursor: for a model without an agent, adapt an existing multi-model headless loop (OpenCode) instead.
payload.chose: Architecture: the driver is a stateless fold over the record. The record is the queue — next task comes from the plan fold, and every launch, handoff (reason: threshold | task_done | stall | needs_user) and stop is an event whose schema lives in packages/schema. Agents are reached through a three-call adapter — launch(digest, task), usage() → tokens, wait() → {exit, wrote_back} — Claude Code first, a second headless agent to prove the contract. Policy is task-scoped by default (one task per session, no context sensor needed, identical on every model); a context threshold is an optional optimisation that packs small tasks into one session. Tasks may carry model/effort hints and the driver routes per task.
payload.over: An in-session orchestrator spawning subagents per task (the orchestrator's context still grows with results, subagents cannot be resumed, and worker write-backs muddle one-session-one-record); a driver that keeps its own run state; a threshold-only policy that depends on vendor usage reporting; or implementing an agent loop inside sofar for models that lack one.
payload.rule: The driver holds no state outside the record and never implements an agent loop of its own — it launches existing headless agents through the adapter, and every driver-side state change is an event in packages/schema.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Exact single-occurrence replace. stdin: OLD block, a line '=====', NEW block."""
import sys
path = sys.argv[1]
data = sys.stdin.read()
old, new = data.split('\n=====\n', 1)
if new.endswith('\n'): new = new[:-1]
if old.endswith('\n'): old = old[:-1]
src = open(path, encoding='utf8').read()
n = src.count(old)
if n != 1:
    sys.exit(f'{path}: expected exactly 1 match, found {n}')
open(path, 'w', encoding='utf8').write(src.replace(old, new, 1))
print(f'{path}: replaced ({len(old)} -> {len(new)} chars)')
PYEOF
echo ok
